title: Graph Network
description: Public-view health of Graph Protocol components, exported by graph-monitor. Nothing here is graded by the tool: it reports what it read, and this dashboard (and its alert rules) decide what is acceptable.

panels.title: Source
panels.description: Up only if every source passed verification: each network's RPC and any subgraph source. Which one is down: see Sources now.

panels.title: Cycle age
panels.description: Seconds since a cycle last read anything. This is the deadman: `up` catches a dead process, this catches one that is alive but wedged.

panels.title: Unreadable
panels.description: Watches that could not read. NOT the same as a bad value — this means the tool is blind, usually a provider limit or an outage.

panels.title: Source lag
panels.description: The worst lag across all sources. Per source: see Sources now.

panels.title: Block
panels.description: Every value on this dashboard was read at these heights, one per network.

panels.title: Version
panels.description: Running build, for lining a change in behaviour up against a deploy.

panels.title: Sources now
panels.description: What graph-monitor reads from: each network's RPC (rpc:<network>) and any subgraph source (subgraph:<label>). Verified every cycle before anything is read through it. Down means the tool is blind to what it serves: every watch on a down RPC's network is unreadable; a down subgraph source makes activity watches fall back to searching the chain.

panels.title: Accounts now

targets.expr: max by (network, group, account, address) (gm_account_eth_balance{network=~"$network", group=~"$group", account=~"$account"})
max by (network, group, account, address) (gm_account_grt_balance{network=~"$network", group=~"$group", account=~"$account"})
max by (network, group, account, address) (gm_account_idle_seconds{network=~"$network", group=~"$group", account=~"$account"})
max by (network, group, account, address) (gm_account_activity_seen{network=~"$network", group=~"$group", account=~"$account"})

panels.description: One row per watched account. Blank cells mean that asset is not watched for that account — not that it is zero.

panels.title: ETH balance
panels.description: Solid lines are balances. A dashed line is that account's configured top-up trigger, shown only where remediation is configured.

panels.title: Time since last activity
panels.description: Time since the account last did the thing it exists to do, measured at the pinned block. A line climbing without resetting is an account that has gone quiet. Log scale, so an account quiet for months does not flatten the ones measured in hours. With a subgraph source, quiet accounts keep a value past their lookback instead of turning unreadable.

panels.title: Not seen in the lookback

targets.expr: max by (network, group, account) (gm_account_activity_seen{network=~"$network", group=~"$group", account=~"$account"}) == 0

max by (network, group, account) (gm_account_idle_seconds{network=~"$network", group=~"$group", account=~"$account"}) and on (network, group, account) (max by (network, group, account) (gm_account_activity_seen{network=~"$network", group=~"$group", account=~"$account"}) == 0)

panels.description: Read successfully, nothing within the account's lookback. Empty is the healthy state, and this is NOT the same as an unreadable watch. Quiet for = time since the last event, when known (a subgraph source knows it past the lookback); blank means no event was ever found.

panels.title: GRT allowances

targets.expr: max by (network, group, owner, spender) (gm_account_allowance_unlimited{network=~"$network", group=~"$group"})
max by (network, group, owner, spender) (gm_account_allowance_exact_max{network=~"$network", group=~"$group"})
max by (network, group, owner, spender) (gm_account_allowance_grt{network=~"$network", group=~"$group"})

panels.description: Use the Unlimited column, not Raw GRT: an unlimited approval is ~1.157e59 and a float cannot represent it faithfully. That column is computed on exact integers.

panels.title: Subgraphs now
panels.description: One row per subgraph check: the published version, plus each listed deployment. Up means it answered, from the expected deployment, without indexing errors and within max_lag. "Not checked" means our side failed (e.g. API key) and says nothing about the subgraph. Blank cells mean that number could not be measured this cycle, not that it is zero. Subgraphs on every chain are listed, not just the selected network; Blocks behind is only measured for the chain graph-monitor's RPC serves.

panels.title: Subgraph lag
panels.description: How far each subgraph's latest indexed block trails the wall clock. A line that stops means the subgraph could not be read.

panels.title: Read failures
panels.description: Rising here while the source stays up usually means a provider limit — block range or rate — rather than an outage.

panels.title: Cycle duration
panels.description: If p95 approaches the serve interval, cycles start skipping ticks.

panels.title: Watch duration p95
panels.description: Activity watches dominate: they scan logs backwards and cost scales with how far back they must look.

panels.title: Remediation outcomes
panels.description: Empty unless --remediate is on. `failed` is the one to alert on: an auto-fix that is broken is more urgent than the balance that triggered it.
